correctness.rationale: Derivations preserve the derived ideal W and satisfy D|_W=ρ(A) by applying the ordinary derivation identity to [u,v]; every B:V→W is allowed at this stage. Squaring D gives A²=0, ρ(A)²=0 and BA+ρ(A)B=0. On decomposable wedges, after A²=0 the middle condition is precisely 2Au∧Av=0. This yields the stated obstruction in odd characteristic; in characteristic two B=0 realizes every rank of a square-zero A. In a Jordan-pair basis Ay_i=x_i, with a complement spanned by z_j, the images from Y∧Z, ∧²Y and X∧Y give independent spaces of dimensions r(n−2r), binom(r,2), binom(r,2), respectively. In particular the ∧²Y images x_i∧y_j−x_j∧y_i have distinct off-diagonal supports, including in characteristic two. The equation for B then lets one choose B(y_i) freely and B(z_j) in ker ρ(A), with B(x_i)=−ρ(A)B(y_i); the equations on x_i are automatic. The flag U=im A⊆K=ker A and invertible map V/K→U give the exact count and include r=0. For geometry the same flags and fiberwise invertible maps describe the reduced rank-r base, smooth and geometrically irreducible. The flag dimensions r(n−r)+r(n−2r) plus the open isomorphism fiber of dimension r² give 2r(n−r). Over that reduced base the B equation is a constant-rank map between trivial vector bundles; locally a maximal minor splits off the image, giving the claimed kernel bundle and reduced smooth stratum in each allowed characteristic. No property of the entire unreduced scheme follows. The frozen checker and recorded output were inspected, not executed; they report finite-field fiber tests and small exhaustive checks, not a general certificate.

evidence: Rank-one central shears with functional zero on W are genuinely common to the square-zero derivation and Nijenhuis sets. Fixed-point-free automorphisms of the same six-dimensional algebra are invertible maps, not derivations in the zero-square fiber.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The common central shears lie in the r=0 quotient stratum and do not exhaust even that stratum. The inspected Nijenhuis and automorphism theorems therefore do not imply the finite-field formula or general geometry. The odd-characteristic obstruction by itself should not be presented as independent novelty. Same-day dates do not settle priority.

evidence: The free-derivation extension description gives the ambient parameters, not the zero-square restriction. Infinitesimal automorphisms 1+εD over ε²=0 correspond to all derivations regardless of D². The differential-module formulation k[t]/(t²), t acting by D, adds bracket compatibility to the linear square-zero condition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither a count of tangent automorphisms nor the unconstrained square-zero endomorphism count imposes both the wedge-square action and the compatible central lift on this algebra. Restricted derivations also impose a different identity.

evidence: Heisenberg rank spectra give the exact excluded n=2 total q³+q²−q. The rank-one Nijenhuis census and the same-family idempotent derivation census are exact but imposed by different equations.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The first claimed family starts at n=3 and is indexed by quotient rank; Heisenberg algebras with one-dimensional derived ideal cannot supply the higher-dimensional exterior-square fibers. Operator rank one in the Nijenhuis table is not quotient rank one, and D²=D is not D²=0.

originality.rationale: The derivation normal form and the general identity giving the odd-characteristic abelian-image obstruction are structural antecedents or standard consequences. The supported distinct result is the uniform census by rank of the quotient map (not total operator rank) and its reduced bundle strata on the free class-two family for n≥3, including the higher-rank characteristic-two fibers. The exact Heisenberg boundary, local-derivation theory and partially overlapping rank-one Nijenhuis operators do not supply this census.
residual_risks: The 2014 free nilpotent Lie algebra survey (DML-CZ 143811) was not retrieved for independent full-text comparison; the structural antecedent is not ruled out from covering more than cited.
The general modular representation or differential-module literature could imply an equivalent enumeration; a bounded unsuccessful query does not establish priority.

value.rationale: The precise quotient-rank distribution in a natural family of derivation algebras distinguishes modular behavior not seen in the tangent-space dimension, and the smooth vector-bundle fibers explain the point counts geometrically. Already at n=4 a rank-two branch appears in characteristic two and is structurally excluded in odd characteristic. The result counts whole families over arbitrary finite fields, not just this boundary witness or a test table.
